issues.description: Blocking read() can hang indefinitely if writer never closes the FIFO
issues.detail: After the first non-empty read, the code unconditionally switches to blocking mode and enters `while True: os.read(fifo_fd, 8192)` with no timeout, no poll, and no liveness check against `command_obj`. If the subprocess writes some data and then hangs (or stalls without closing the FIFO), the parent will block forever inside the inner loop — the very protections the original code carried (select poll timeout, check_process_exited) are bypassed. This regresses the documented goals 'Can detect subprocess failures early / Can timeout if subprocess hangs' for any call after the first byte arrives.

issues.description: Loop no longer terminates when subprocess exits without writing (deadlock on poll timeout path)
issues.detail: The previous code handled the 'poll returned no events, read returned empty' case by checking `check_process_exited(command_obj)` and breaking when the process had already exited (a MacOS-specific symptom called out in the removed comment). The new code replaces that branch with `pass`, so if the writer dies after producing content but the kernel never signals EOF/BlockingIOError on the reader fd (the original macOS bug), the outer loop spins forever. The final `if not content and check_process_exited(...)` outside the loop is unreachable in this scenario because `content` is non-empty.

issues.description: F_SETFL not wrapped in try/finally; fd left in blocking mode on exception
issues.detail: `fcntl.fcntl(fifo_fd, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags & ~os.O_NONBLOCK)` mutates shared fd state. If a subsequent `os.read` raises (e.g. OSError, KeyboardInterrupt) or the caller reuses the fd, it is silently left blocking. A try/finally that restores the original flags before returning would make the side effect local and safer.

issues.description: Dead variable `has_blocking_error` likely still referenced elsewhere or now misleading
issues.detail: The previous code set `has_blocking_error = True` inside the except branch. The new code removes the assignment but the surrounding function (not shown in diff) may still initialize or inspect that flag. Either way the variable name and its initialization above the loop become dead state. Confirm and remove or the reader is left with a vestigial control variable.

issues.description: Busy-spin when no data and no events
issues.detail: Both the `else` (no poll events) and `except BlockingIOError` branches now just `pass`, so the outer `while` loop will tight-loop calling `select.poll()` and `os.read()` with no backoff until the first byte arrives. If `select.poll()` was called with a non-zero timeout this is fine, but if the timeout is short or zero (not shown), this becomes a CPU hot loop. Worth verifying the poll timeout is meaningful and adding a short sleep / relying on poll to block.

issues.description: POSIX guarantee cited in the PR does not strictly apply to all FIFO/pipe edge cases on macOS
issues.detail: The justification rests on 'blocking read() returns 0 only after writer closes AND buffers are drained'. This is true for pipes/FIFOs on POSIX *once there has ever been a writer with the FIFO open*. If multiple writers exist, or if the subprocess re-opens the FIFO, blocking read can return 0 prematurely between writers. Given the PR exists specifically to fix a flaky FIFO race, it's worth confirming there is exactly one writer lifecycle and documenting that invariant in the code comment.

issues.description: No new test covers the truncated-JSON race the PR is meant to fix
issues.detail: The diff contains only the fix. A regression test that writes >64KB to a FIFO from a subprocess and exits immediately would have reproduced the original bug deterministically (or with high probability under load) and would protect against future reverts. Worth adding under `test/runner/`.

issues.description: Inner loop loses ability to surface partial content on subprocess crash mid-stream
issues.detail: If the writer crashes after sending a partial JSON payload, the new blocking loop will eventually see EOF and return whatever `content` was accumulated — which the caller will then try to `json.loads()` and fail with the same error class the PR is trying to eliminate. Consider validating completeness (e.g. length-prefix or trailing sentinel) rather than relying solely on EOF semantics.

issues.description: Import of `fcntl` makes the module Unix-only
issues.detail: `fcntl` is not available on Windows. If `metaflow/runner/utils.py` is imported on Windows (even paths that don't call `read_from_fifo_when_ready`), the top-level `import fcntl` will fail. Either guard the import or document the platform constraint. Metaflow already has Linux/macOS-only paths, but this should be a conscious choice.

dissents.topic: Should the fix switch to blocking mode at all, or just retry/drain in non-blocking mode?

positions.position: Switching to blocking mode is the cleanest way to get the kernel's guaranteed drain-then-EOF semantics; trying to emulate that with non-blocking + polling is the source of the original bug.

Keep non-blocking + poll, but loop until BOTH `check_process_exited` is true AND a subsequent read returns 0 AND poll reports no events for N consecutive iterations. This preserves timeout/liveness detection that the blocking inner loop throws away.

dissents.topic: Severity of losing the macOS-specific exit check

positions.position: Once we're in blocking mode after the first byte, the macOS quirk in the removed comment can't trigger — the kernel will deliver EOF correctly. So removing the explicit check_process_exited branch is fine.

The removed branch protected the pre-first-byte path too implicitly via the outer loop. Now if the subprocess exits before writing anything OR after writing zero-and-then-hanging, behavior diverges. Keep an explicit liveness gate.
The PR is narrowly targeted, easy to review, and addresses the dominant failure mode (large JSON truncation). Ship it; iterate on tests separately.

Relying on FIFO EOF to delimit a JSON message is fragile by construction. The real fix is a length-prefixed or newline-delimited framing protocol so partial reads are detectable. The blocking-mode change papers over a protocol smell.

review.summary: The PR correctly identifies a real race (non-blocking read + early EOF detection truncates large JSON payloads on FIFOs) and the blocking-mode-after-first-byte strategy is a defensible fix. However, the implementation gives up two safety properties the original code had: (1) timeout/liveness detection during the bulk of the read, because the inner `while True: os.read(...)` has no poll or process-exit check and can hang forever if the writer stalls without closing; and (2) recovery from the macOS-specific 'no EOF, no BlockingIOError' case during the initial wait, which the diff replaces with `pass`. Two P0 blockers (potential indefinite hang, regressed macOS exit-detection path) plus minor hygiene issues (fcntl not in try/finally, no regression test, Windows import). Recommend adding a liveness check inside the blocking inner loop (e.g. periodic poll with timeout or a separate watchdog) and restoring the `check_process_exited` branch in the outer loop before merging.
